policy: Prefer primary standards and reference-data institutions. Every evidence reference resolves to a revisioned entry with a source locator and access state. Source-corpus claims remain labeled and never inherit validation from a traditional comparison.

policyAttribution.sourceLocator: Claim and provenance vocabulary; Content architecture
caveats: This policy governs Tour attribution and does not certify the scientific quality of a cited source.

entries.title: OpenSimPhy Physics Tour Master Plan
entries.sourceLocator: Claim and provenance vocabulary; Content architecture; Scientific and content contracts
entries.scopeNote: Internal authority for Tour scope, attribution inheritance, source-time result status, conclusion boundaries, and the distinction between content readiness and implementation delivery.
entries.licenseNote: Repository policy document; project license and repository history govern reuse.

entries.title: The International System of Units (SI)
entries.responsibleOrganization: Bureau International des Poids et Mesures
entries.sourceLocator: Sections 2.2-2.3 and Appendix 2; defining constants, unit definitions, and practical realizations
entries.scopeNote: Current authority used for SI defining constants, conventional ISQ base quantities, units, and the distinction between definitions and practical realizations.

entries.title: Conventional Values of the Josephson and von Klitzing Constants: CIPM Recommendations 1 and 2 (1988)
entries.responsibleOrganization: International Committee for Weights and Measures
entries.revision: Adopted in 1988 for use from 1 January 1990
entries.sourceLocator: Recommendation 1, conventional value K_J-90 = 483 597.9 GHz/V; Recommendation 2, conventional value R_K-90 = 25 812.807 ohm
entries.scopeNote: Primary authority for the exact conventional K_J-90 and R_K-90 values used from 1 January 1990. These historical practical values are not current SI defining values.
entries.licenseNote: Official BIPM publication; consult BIPM terms for reuse.

entries.title: International Vocabulary of Metrology - Basic and General Concepts and Associated Terms (VIM)
entries.responsibleOrganization: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology
entries.sourceLocator: Entries 1.1 quantity, 1.2 kind of quantity, 1.7 quantity dimension, 1.19 quantity value, 1.20 numerical quantity value, and 1.26 ordinal quantity
entries.scopeNote: Terminology authority for separating quantity, quantity kind, quantity dimension, quantity value, and numerical quantity value; entry 1.26 bounds the treatment of ordinal quantities.
entries.licenseNote: Copyright is jointly held by the JCGM member organizations; consult JCGM 200:2012 for reproduction permissions.

entries.title: Guide for the Use of the International System of Units (SI)
entries.responsibleOrganization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
entries.sourceLocator: Chapters 4, 7, and 8 and Appendix B; page warning above the abbreviated table of contents
entries.scopeNote: Notation and multiplicative conversion guidance only. The NIST page visibly warns that SP 811 has not been updated for the SI changes effective 20 May 2019; use the current BIPM brochure for present SI definitions.
entries.licenseNote: NIST publication; reuse is subject to NIST copyright and website policies.

entries.title: CODATA recommended values of the fundamental physical constants: 2022
entries.responsibleOrganization: CODATA Task Group on Fundamental Constants
entries.sourceLocator: Recommended-values tables, correlations, and discussion of the 2022 least-squares adjustment
entries.scopeNote: Measured constants, standard uncertainties, and correlations from the 2022 adjustment. SI defining constants are exact and are not independent measured evidence.
entries.licenseNote: Published by the American Physical Society; consult the journal record for reuse terms.

entries.title: University Physics Volume 3
entries.revision: Published 29 September 2016; web content accessed 27 July 2026
entries.sourceLocator: Sections 5.8-5.9, 6.1, 6.3-6.5, 8.1-8.3, and 8.5; relativistic particle scales, black-body radiation, Compton and de Broglie relations, hydrogen structure and spectra, magnetic moments, and electron spin
entries.scopeNote: Textbook model reference for relativistic particle scales, matter waves, hydrogen-like spectra, magnetic moments and spin, and ideal black-body radiation. CODATA and BIPM remain authoritative for current constant values and SI definitions.
entries.licenseNote: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) for the cited textbook content; OpenStax trademarks and covers are excluded.

entries.title: Quantities, Units and Symbols in Physical Chemistry
entries.responsibleOrganization: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry
entries.revision: Corrected 2nd printing, 2008; searchable online PDF released December 2012
entries.sourceLocator: Sections 2.10-2.11 and 4.3; amount of substance, molar quantities, ideal-gas relationships, and standard-state conventions
entries.scopeNote: Terminology and symbols authority for amount of substance, molar quantities, ideal-gas relationships, and explicit state conventions. Current SI definitions are checked against the current BIPM SI Brochure.
entries.licenseNote: Copyright IUPAC and the Royal Society of Chemistry; the authoritative PDF is publicly accessible, but reproduction remains subject to the publisher and IUPAC terms.

entries.title: Re-definition of the Astronomical Unit of Length: IAU 2012 Resolution B2
entries.sourceLocator: Resolution B2, paragraphs 1-2; astronomical unit defined exactly as 149 597 870 700 m
entries.scopeNote: Primary authority for the exact metre value of the astronomical unit. Derived parsec and light-year catalog values retain their separately declared geometrical or time-distance relationships.
entries.licenseNote: Official IAU resolution; consult IAU publication terms for reuse.

entries.title: Nominal Values for Selected Solar and Planetary Quantities: IAU 2015 Resolution B3
entries.sourceLocator: Resolution rationale and Tables 1-2; nominal solar, terrestrial, and jovian conversion constants
entries.scopeNote: Authority for exact nominal solar and planetary conversion constants. Nominal constants are conversion factors and are not measured current-best properties of the Sun or planets.
entries.licenseNote: Published by the American Astronomical Society on behalf of the IAU; consult the journal record for reuse terms.
